newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Keramik Laufen sees strong 1997 improvement.
newsitem.headline: Keramik Laufen sees strong 1997 improvement.

text.p: Keramik Holding AG Laufen said it was confident the group would show a strong improvement in 1997 results and first quarter business confirmed this view.
Keramik Laufen, which makes tiles, sanitary ware and ceramics, said confidence for 1997 was based on the group's restructuring and efforts to improve capacity and productivity.

"In view of the restructuring and our efforts to date to expand capacity and improve productivity, we are confident that we will report a strong improvement in the 1997 result," chief executive Erich Stiefelmeyer told a news conference.

In 1996 Keramik Laufen's group net profit fell to 30 million Swiss francs from 52 million and the board will propose an unchanged dividend of 15 francs per bearer share and three francs per registered share.
Sales rose 6.4 percent to 945 million francs and cash flow fell to 110 million from 124 million.

Keramik Laufen said the poor result was due to the weak state of Central Europe's construction industry and restructuring measures, but results from Keramik Laufen's other markets -- Eastern Europe, North America and Brazil in the second half -- were good.
The group result was helped by satisfactory financial earnings and extraordinary revenues.
